- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid missing downside momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day mean in early forecast windows; apply 3–5% downward bias for first 10 days of forecast horizon.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.5, -1.0, +0.5), model fails to mean-revert; apply smoothing filter to dampen volatility in middle forecast days.
- When sentiment is flat (0.0–0.25) for 3+ consecutive days, model drifts toward historical mean; adjust forecast to align with 10-day rolling average of past 30d.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in 10–15 day horizon; reduce forecast slope for days 10–15 if sentiment is neutral or negative.
